articles.title: NITI Aayog and GIZ India Sign Implementation Agreement under Nationally Determined Contribution-Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) to Accelerate Road Freight Decarbonisation
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH signed an Implementation Agreement under the Nationally Determined Contribution–Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) on 3 rd November 2026. NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German Government's International Climate Initiative (IKI). World Resources Institute (WRI) India, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India and Agora Energiewende are among the initiative's implementing partners.
Decarbonising road freight is an important component of India's transition towards a sustainable, energy-efficient and low-carbon transport system. However, the electrification of medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles remains at an early stage, highlighting the need for adequate charging infrastructure, innovative financing mechanisms and an enabling regulatory framework. The Agreement formalises the collaboration between the project partners for accelerating the decarbonisation of India's road freight sector. The initiative will contribute to India's broader efforts to achieve its Nationally Determined Contribution targets and long-term climate goals.
articles.summary: NITI Aayog and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH signed an Implementation Agreement under the Nationally Determined Contribution–Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) on 3 rd November 2026. NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German Government's International Climate Initiative (IKI). World Resources Institute (WRI) India, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India and Agora Energiewende are among the initiative's implementing partners.

India to pursue Solution-oriented and Equitable Climate Action at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya: Union Environment Minister
articles.full_content:
Predictable Climate Finance, Party-Driven Mitigation and Adaptation Outcomes, Technology Transfer and Just Transition to be India's Focus: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, outlined India’s priorities for COP31 of the UNFCCC, to be held in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 th to 20 th November 2026, and highlighted the key outcomes of India’s participation in CBD COP17 and UNCCD COP17. Briefing the media in New Delhi today the Minister said India will approach COP31 with a solution-oriented vision, bringing practical solutions for the Global South, with capacity building, knowledge sharing and geography-specific solutions at the core. India will work closely with G-77 and China, LMDC and BASIC, he informed.
The Minister reaffirmed that India stands committed to make positive contributions to global efforts to achieve objectives of climate convention and goals of Paris Agreement. He said Climate finance will be a key priority, with India seeking a COP31 decision to commence the Climate Finance Work Programme. Shri Yadav emphasised that finance is an obligation of developed countries under Article 9.1 and must be predictable, largely public and concessional, and should not add to the debt burden. India will also press for mitigation and the Global Stocktake to remain Party-driven, facilitative and non-punitive, respecting the nationally determined nature of NDCs and ruling out new top-down targets.
Further, the Minister informed that Adaptation will remain a priority for India, with Global Goal on Adaptation indicators being voluntary and not conditioning access to finance, alongside scaled-up adaptation finance. India will support continuation of the Just Transition Work Programme through a Party-driven mechanism, viewing just transition through the lens of climate justice, the right to development and affordable energy access. On technology, India will emphasise that technology transfer is an obligation of developed countries and that barriers related to cost, IPR and trade must be addressed. Participation in carbon markets should remain voluntary. India will also underline that voluntary initiatives under the Presidency Action Agenda should remain separate from negotiations and that uniform global targets must respect national circumstances.
India will also highlight the linkage between the need for adaptation in agriculture, food security and the livelihoods of small and marginal farmers. Its engagements at COP31 will include LeadIT 3.0 with Sweden, in addition to high-level side events on coastal resilience, panels on IBCA and forests. Shri Yadav said India will play a constructive, bridge-building role in Antalya, seeking an outcome that moves from commitments to implementation and support.

NITI Aayog and TEXMiN Sign Joint Statement of Intent to Strengthen India’s Critical Minerals Ecosystem
articles.full_content:
Prof. Gobardhan Das highlights the strategic importance of critical minerals for national security, technological self-reliance and Viksit Bharat 2047
NITI Aayog and TEXMiN (Technology Translation Research Park), an initiative of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, signed a Joint Statement of Intent (SoI) to strengthen collaboration in the critical and strategic minerals sector.
The collaboration aims to advance indigenous technological capabilities, promote research & innovation and support the development of resilient and sustainable critical mineral value chains in India. It aligns with the objectives of the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM) and the vision of an Aatmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat.
The SoI was signed during the visit of Prof. Gobardhan Das, Member, NITI Aayog, to IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, where he inaugurated the National Symposium on Critical Minerals and Rare Earths (CMRE 2026) on 31 October 2026, organised as part of the 45 th Annual National Conference of the Indian Council of Chemists.
Addressing the symposium, Prof. Das highlighted the importance of critical minerals as strategic enablers of national security, technological self-reliance and India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Drawing on India’s rich metallurgical heritage, he emphasised the need to build indigenous technological capabilities through research, innovation and industry collaboration.
He stressed the need to move beyond a mine-centric approach towards an integrated value chain encompassing exploration, processing, refining, advanced materials and recycling. He also highlighted the potential of recovering critical minerals from secondary resources such as coal fly ash, red mud, mine tailings and electronic waste, while underscoring the importance of translating research into commercially viable technologies and promoting sustainable resource utilisation.
The Joint Statement of Intent between NITI Aayog and TEXMiN envisages cooperation in four key areas: collaborative research and technology development; technical and strategic studies; policy and institutional support; and capacity building and knowledge exchange.
The collaboration aims to strengthen indigenous capabilities, facilitate technology translation and promote stronger linkages among government, academia, research institutions and industry.
The symposium brought together policymakers, researchers, technology developers and industry representatives to deliberate on strengthening India’s critical minerals and rare earths ecosystem.
The initiative is expected to contribute to India’s efforts towards building resilient critical mineral supply chains and advancing technological self-reliance.Ll

articles.title: Ministry of MSME observes Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 on the Theme of “Probity for Prosperity”
articles.full_content:
Nukkad Natak Organised to promote Integrity and Preventive Vigilance during Vigilance Awareness Week 2026
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) observed Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 from 26th October to 1st November 2026, in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This year’s theme was “Probity for Prosperity” (सत्यनिष्ठा से समृद्धि). In line with the Commission’s advisory, the Ministry also undertook a three-month preventive vigilance campaign from 17th August to 16th November 2026, focusing on expeditious disposal of pending complaints and cases, capacity-building programmes, digital initiatives, and contract management.
The week-long observance commenced on 26th October 2026 with the Secretary, Ministry of MSME, Shri Bharat Khera, administering the Integrity Pledge to the officers and staff of the Ministry at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi. More than 500 officials from the Ministry and its organisations participated in the pledge-taking ceremony in hybrid mode, reaffirming their commitment to integrity, transparency and probity in public service.
As part of the observance, Quiz and Slogan Writing competitions were organised for the officials of the Ministry on 26th October 2026. The competitions witnessed enthusiastic participation and aimed at fostering greater awareness of integrity, transparency, probity and ethical conduct in the discharge of official responsibilities.
The central event marking the culmination of the week-long observance was held on 30th October 2026 under the Chair of Secretary. The event was attended by more than 300 officials of the Ministry and its organisations and field offices across the country through hybrid mode. On the occasion, the Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO), MSME, made a presentation highlighting the preventive vigilance initiatives undertaken by the Ministry during the three-month campaign. Secretary (MSME) also felicitated the winners of the Quiz and Slogan Writing competitions and emphasised the importance of imbibing the values of integrity, transparency and accountability embodied in the theme “Probity for Prosperity”.
Further reinforcing the message of vigilance and ethical conduct, a Nukkad Natak was staged by a team from the National School of Drama (NSD) on 30th October 2026 at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi. Based on the theme “Probity for Prosperity”, the performance highlighted the importance of adherence to Conduct Rules, continuous upgradation of knowledge and effective use of the whistleblower mechanism in preventing and combating corruption. More than 300 officials from various Ministries and Departments witnessed the performance.
Through the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 and the ongoing preventive vigilance campaign, the Ministry of MSME reiterated its commitment to strengthening transparency, accountability and integrity in governance. articles.full_content:
The Press Information Bureau , Chennai, in collaboration with the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB), organised a Media Workshop on “Promoting Environment-Friendly Lifestyles” on 03 November 2026 in Chennai. The workshop was inaugurated by Dr. V. K. Rajeev, Minister for Environment and Climate Change, Government of Tamil Nadu. The programme focused on sustainable lifestyles, circular economy, environmental protection and eco-friendly celebrations, with participation from government officials, environmental experts and media representatives.
Addressing the gathering, the Minister urged the public to celebrate festivals without causing harm to the environment. Emphasising the need to avoid harmful chemicals in the manufacture of firecrackers during Deepavali, he encouraged the use of green crackers manufactured in accordance with the guidelines of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research - National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI). He also advised the public to purchase only crackers bearing the green cracker logo and verify their authenticity through the QR code.
Pointing out that air and noise pollution caused by firecrackers adversely affect children and people with respiratory ailments, the Minister urged the public to adhere to the time restrictions prescribed by the Government. He announced that solar lights would be provided to villages located near bird sanctuaries that have voluntarily refrained from bursting firecrackers for several years. He also stated that large-scale plantation of trees suitable for birds would be undertaken in these villages.
The Minister stressed the need to reduce plastic usage and adopt biodegradable alternatives. Conveying the message, “Celebrate more, pollute less”, he urged the public to celebrate Deepavali in an environment-friendly manner.
Shri. Anurag Mishra, Chairman, Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, in his special address, highlighted the importance of environmental protection, sustainable use of natural resources, responsible consumption and waste reduction. He emphasised that public participation and media-led awareness initiatives were essential to creating a clean and green environment.

Kamaraj, Additional Director General, Press Information Bureau, Chennai, highlighted the important role of the media in taking environmental awareness to the public. He noted that journalists play a vital role in communicating scientific and technological information in a simple and accessible manner and in encouraging public participation in environmental protection.

Spices Board Chairperson holds discussions with World Bank and IFC on strengthening the spices value chain
articles.full_content:
New Delhi, 3 November 2026: Adv. Sangeetha Viswanathan, Chairperson, Spices Board, attended a stakeholder consultation with representatives of the World Bank and the International Finance Corporation (IFC), organised by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) under its Technical Assistance on “Enhancing Job Creation and Competitiveness in India’s Food Processing Sector”.
Discussions were held on strengthening the existing common infrastructure for the spices sector. The possibility of IFC extending financial support for developing and strengthening an end-to-end spices value chain, with a potential Public-Private Partnership (PPP) implementation model, was also explored.
The Chairperson stressed that safe and traceable spices must be ensured from the farm level, through introduction of technology, traceability, reduced use of pesticides, lower cost of production and skilled labour.
The IFC team expressed its interest in holding further discussions with the Spices Board to explore the proposal in greater detail.

Ministry of Mines Concludes Special Campaign 6 with Significant Achievements in E-Waste Management, Cleanliness and Governance
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Mines, along with its attached and subordinate offices, Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and autonomous bodies, has successfully concluded Special Campaign 6, with a particular focus on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste. The campaign also focused on cleanliness, efficient record management, disposal of pending references, resolution of public grievances and improving administrative efficiency, reaffirming the Ministry's commitment to sustainability and good governance.
A key highlight of Special Campaign 6 was the extensive drive for the collection and disposal of e-waste. During the campaign, a total of 134.92 tonnes of e-waste had been collected/disposed across 96 locations, generating revenue of approx ₹ 1.2 crore. The initiative covered offices of the Ministry of Mines / field offices as well as other government offices, promoting the responsible disposal of electronic waste, resource recovery and environmentally sustainable practices.
During the campaign period, 465 cleanliness campaign were conducted across the Ministry and its organizations. The campaign generated total revenue of approximately 6.19 crore from disposal of scrap and e-waste, and freed approximately 47881 square feet of office space. These efforts contributed to improved workplace conditions, better utilization of office space and the promotion of a culture of cleanliness and sustainability.
Under the record management initiative, 13067 physical files were reviewed, of which 9470 were weeded out. In the electronic records category, 3270 e-files were reviewed and 1812 were closed. Overall 11282 files were weeded out or closed, contributing to streamlined record management and improved administrative efficiency.
The Ministry also achieved its targets in disposing the Public Grievances/ Public Grievances appeals, references received from Members of Parliament, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO), the Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) and State Governments reference. In addition, 7 rules/processes were simplified during the campaign to promote ease of governance and administrative efficiency.
Several innovative best practices were undertaken by the Ministry's organisations to promote environmental sustainability and resource conservation. Green Hydrogen
articles.full_content:
Emerging Pillar of India’s Clean Energy Transition
Green hydrogen is emerging as a pillar of India’s clean energy transition. It is produced by splitting water using renewable electricity. It can help reduce emissions in sectors such as fertiliser production, petroleum refining, iron and steel manufacturing, heavy-duty road transport and shipping . The National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) supports domestic manufacturing, production, assured demand and credible certification. From green ammonia auctions to India’s first hydrogen train, early projects point to a promising path.
Why Green Hydrogen
Hydrogen is an energy carrier that stores energy and delivers it for varied uses. In a fuel cell, it reacts with oxygen to produce electricity, leaving only water and heat as by-products, and no polluting compounds or greenhouse gases.Although pure hydrogen is not found in large quantities in nature, it can be extracted from compounds such as water or natural gas. Its environmental impact therefore depends on how it is made. Conventional methods rely on fossil fuels and release carbon emissions.
Production using renewable electricity from solar and wind power can cut this footprint substantially. Hydrogen made by splitting water using renewable power is called green hydrogen . Unlike fossil-based routes, this process emits far less carbon. India’s abundant solar and wind resources make domestic production feasible. This diversifies the country’s energy sources and strengthens energy security.
It also supports India’s goal of net-zero emissions by 2070.Green hydrogen matters most in sectors where cutting emissions is difficult. Reasons include high-temperature heat needs, chemical processes and few alternatives to fossil fuels. These hard-to-abate sectors include fertiliser, petroleum refining, iron and steel, heavy-duty road transport and shipping. Fertiliser and refining plants already use hydrogen, so green hydrogen can replace the fossil-based supply. It can also support lower-emission steelmaking, selected transport uses and energy storage. It is especially useful where direct electrification is difficult or less practical.
What Makes Hydrogen “Green”
Hydrogen releases no carbon dioxide when used, so its climate impact depends on how it is produced. In August 2023, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) notified India’s Green Hydrogen Standard. Hydrogen qualifies as green if emissions do not exceed 2 kg of CO₂ equivalent per kg of hydrogen, on a well-to-gate basis, measured as a 12-month average. India thus became one of the first few countries to define green hydrogen formally.
For India, wider adoption could reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels. It would also lessen exposure to global fuel price swings. The sector could open opportunities in manufacturing, draw investment, create jobs and expand exports. Building capabilities across the value chain would strengthen domestic supply chains and spur industrial innovation. Green hydrogen

articles.full_content:
DPIIT Disposes of Over 99% of Public Grievances and Closes 83% of Identified E-Files Under Special Campaign 6
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), along with its attached and subordinate offices, is implementing Special Campaign 6 under the guidance of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG). The campaign aims to institutionalise Swachhata and minimise pendency in official work across all offices.
During the implementation phase, DPIIT has made significant progress across multiple parameters. All categories of pending references, including those received from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), Cabinet, Members of Parliament, State Governments and Public Grievances (PG)/PG Appeals, have been identified and are being systematically addressed to ensure their timely and effective disposal.
As of 28 October 2026, DPIIT has successfully disposed of more than 50% of references received from the PMO, around 75% of references from the Cabinet/Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) and State Governments, over 99% of Public Grievances and more than 80% of Public Grievance Appeals. The Department has also closed around 83% of the identified e-files, reflecting its efforts towards efficient record management. These initiatives have contributed to improving workplace cleanliness and the overall working environment for officials and staff.
The implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, being conducted from 2 to 31 October 2026, was preceded by a preparatory phase from 15 to 30 September 2026. The campaign has helped raise awareness among government officials about the importance of cleanliness, efficient record management and the timely disposal of pending matters. DPIIT remains committed to institutionalising Swachhata and minimising pendency across its attached and subordinate offices, thereby fostering a cleaner, more efficient and responsive working environment.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Addressing the gathering of industry leaders, investors, startup representatives, and senior officials from India and abroad, the Prime Minister noted that this year's summit takes place amid special circumstances dominated by global energy shocks that have underscored the vital importance of renewable energy in daily life and national development. He pointed out that the scope of this year's event is exceptionally broad as it coincides with the Ninth Assembly of the International Solar Alliance and includes delegates from the Fourth Conference on Green Hydrogen.
Stating that recent global disruptions have demonstrated the direct link between energy security and economic security, the Prime Minister warned that continued over-reliance on fossil fuels will repeatedly disrupt the world economy because fossil reserves are finite and concentrated in a few regions. He contrasted this vulnerability with the boundless, universally accessible potential of clean energy. “And we all know, the future of Energy Security lies in Clean Energy,” asserted Shri Modi.
Stating that the new era of the solar revolution relies on innovation as much as adoption, the Prime Minister urged startups, IITs, innovators, and entrepreneurs to design round-the-clock, all-weather solar models capable of meeting maximum household needs, including rooftop solar cooking to minimize reliance on imported gas and home solar charging for electric two-wheelers and cars. “Through this, middle-class families of the country can save thousands of rupees every year,” noted Shri Modi.
Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy, Education and Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Shri Pralhad Joshi, highlighted India's remarkable progress in the renewable energy sector and the transformative role of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's leadership in shaping the country's energy landscape, while addressing the event.
At the outset, the Union Minister expressed his appreciation for the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, stating that he had given India's energy sector a new energy, direction and confidence.
He further highlighted that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi approved the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana with an outlay of more than ₹5,000 crore, under which 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity will be developed. He also noted that the Prime Minister had recently approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III, with an investment of ₹1.86 lakh crore.

articles.title: National Conference on “Gender Data and Statistics: From Evidence to Policy Insights | MoSPI and UN Women
articles.full_content:
A one-day National Conference on “Gender Data and Statistics: From Evidence to Policy Insights” was organised by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in collaboration with UN Women on 2 nd November, 2026 in New Delhi. The conference brought together policymakers, representatives from Central Ministries/Departments and State Governments, statisticians, researchers, academic institutions, technical experts and representatives of UN agencies to deliberate on strengthening the analysis and use of gender statistics for evidence-based policymaking.
The conference was organised to deliberate on and disseminate the findings of Women and Men in India 2025 , a flagship publication of MoSPI, with the aim of deepening the understanding of key findings and their interlinkages across sectors, facilitating discussions among ministries and other stakeholders, and identifying opportunities to strengthen the analytical and policy use of gender statistics.
The conference commenced with a welcome address by Ms. Shoko Ishikawa , Country Representative, UN Women India, who emphasised the importance of gender-disaggregated data and bridging the gap between data producers and users. Mr. Jean-Eric Paque , Ambassador of the European Union (EU) to India, highlighted the EU–India Strategic Partnership in advancing gender equality and women’s economic participation. Dr. Preetam B. Yashvant , Joint Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development, also addressed the gathering, followed by Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI , who emphasised identifying gender gaps to inform evidence-based policies. Dr. Shamika Ravi , Member, Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, highlighted progress in welfare delivery and women’s financial empowerment, while stressing the need for improved employment quality, state-level analysis and stronger gender statistics to guide policy reforms. The inaugural session concluded with a vote of thanks by Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, MoSPI , who acknowledged the contributions of speakers, participants and UN Women.
The conference featured four thematic technical sessions , focusing on health and survival across the life course; girls’ education, learning and transition; women’s work, wages, formality and care; and women’s livelihoods, enterprises, skills and financial inclusion. The sessions brought together experts, policymakers and practitioners to examine key findings from Women and Men in India 2025 , identify differences in outcomes between women and men, and explore opportunities for translating statistical evidence into actionable policy insights.
Discussions on health and survival recognised progress in maternal healthcare and essential health services, while highlighting nutritional and adolescent health challenges. articles.summary: MoU exchanged between MSDE and Government of Assam for setting up of SIIC; Numaligarh Refinery and Oil India Limited clusters declared under PM-SETU The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India, organised a programme on Skilling for International Mobility & PM-SETU', with a special focus on the Tourism and Hospitality sector in Guwahati today. The programme brought together senior representatives of the Central and Assam Governments, industry stakeholders and the skilling ecosystem to deliberate on strengthening the North-Eastern Region's skilling infrastructure, expanding international employment opportunities for its youth and fostering industry-led transformation of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) under the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU). The programme highlighted the immense potential of the North-Eastern Region in tourism and hospitality, particularly in the context of the growing demand for skilled professionals in domestic and international markets.
